messages.subject: factor loadings in CFA
parts:
Hello everyone,

i thought, if i fix the factor variance in a cfa-model to 1, the estimates can be interpreted like correlations and resemble "factor loadings".

However, when i run

HS.model <- 'visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
             textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
             speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9'

fit <- cfa(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939, std.lv=TRUE)
summary(fit)

the estimate of x5 on textual is 1.102. Shouldn't this be <1? Or is this not a correlation?

Thanks, Hans

messages.author: 71bfb5f1e96782a8
messages.subject: Re: factor loadings in CFA
parts:
You are right. I found the answer in Browns CFA book, where it says that you need to standardize the latent AND the observed variable to m = 0, sd = 1 to obtain correlations. Makes sense.

So in lavaan, one could also use cfa(model, data, std.lv = TRUE, std.ov = TRUE)

Thanks a lot, best, hans

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: factor loadings in CFA
parts:
On Fri, Sep 21, 2012 at 10:16 AM, Dr. Hans Hansen <bea...@gmx.de> wrote:
> You are right. I found the answer in Browns CFA book, where it says that you
> need to standardize the latent AND the observed variable to m = 0, sd = 1 to
> obtain correlations. Makes sense.
>
> So in lavaan, one could also use cfa(model, data, std.lv = TRUE, std.ov =
> TRUE)

One could, but there is no need. You can simply use cfa(model, data),
without the std.lv and std.ov flags, but then use summary(fit,
standardized=TRUE) to get the standardized solution (in the last
column).

Yves.
